privacyDetails.title: How it works
privacyDetails.body: Your photo stays in browser memory and is not sent to our server during compression. Opening the site still downloads the page as usual. For visit stats we may use Google Analytics: page, device type, button clicks — not file names or pixels. Language choice may be remembered in the browser. Analytics cookies are Google’s; you can limit them in browser settings. You can also press Offline in the header to cache this language’s tool pages and engines on your device; your files are still not uploaded.

meta.title: What's in the file
meta.localNote: The check runs only on your device — the file is never uploaded.
meta.gpsWarn: This file has a shoot location (GPS) — the photo can reveal where it was taken.
meta.noneFound: No hidden location or camera data found.
meta.stripped: Hidden data removed: no shoot location or camera tags in the result.
meta.hintGps: Keep Remove metadata on and download — location and service tags will be gone.
meta.hintClean: No shoot location found; processing can still strip service tags from the file.
meta.techBody: Output is encoded in the browser (Canvas API → toBlob); EXIF/GPS segments are not copied into the new file. Check: open DevTools → Network while processing — only site static assets (HTML/JS/CSS) load; your image body is not uploaded to our origin.
meta.techBodyPdfCompress: PDF pages are rendered with PDF.js into Canvas, encoded as JPEG, and rebuilt with pdf-lib. After strong compression, text is usually not selectable. While processing, Network only shows site static assets — your PDF body is not uploaded to our origin.
meta.techBodyPdfSanitize: Pages are copied into a new PDFDocument (pdf-lib); Info metadata fields are cleared. Check Network — no file-body upload.

redact.hint: Draw areas — hiding appears instantly. Processing stays in the browser.
redact.fileInMemory: File is in browser memory. During processing the photo body is not uploaded to a server.
